edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Social engagement continuously taxes language, memory, and executive circuits, which is why it is often framed as a contributor to cognitive reserve.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2024 Posis cohort in J Alzheimers Dis, which ties high social engagement to age-related cognitive decline in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
